newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar floats up on raft of positive comment.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar floats up on raft of positive comment.

text.p: The dollar firmed against the mark in Europe on Thursday after a raft of comments from German, U.S. and Japanese officials that they were comfortable with a strengthening U.S. currency.

On the European bourses, leading shares in London and Paris fell back from opening highs and closed flat. Frankfurt was the exception, ending late electronic trading at a record high after Wall Street moved up again after its sixth consecutive record close overnight.

Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer was the latest to add his voice to an international chorus of dollar-friendly comments welcoming the the U.S. currency's recent rally and saying he "would not mind if it were to go a little further".

Earlier, Japan's "Mr Yen", senior finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, said he welcomed a rising dollar and U.S. Treasury Under-secretary Jeffrey Shafer said on Wednesday the policy of the new Clinton administration still favoured dollar strength.

"It's a concerted effort. I don't quite know why they need to talk the dollar up here, but they're certainly doing a successful job," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank in London.
The dollar pushed to a session high of 1.5117 marks and settled at 1.5095 by 1645 GMT, up from late Wednesday's European level of 1.5041.

But dollar/yen went the other way, dropping to a session low of 111.20. Traders said it was depressed by cross rate trading between the mark and the yen, in which the Japanese currency slipped below key support at 73.85 to the mark.
U.S. data issued on Thursday painted an inflation-benign picture, which analysts said backed the Federal Open Market Committee's decision on Wednesday to leave U.S. rates on hold.
October consumer prices rose 0.3 percent on the month and 3.0 on the year, with core CPI up 0.2 percent and 2.6. The numbers matched economists' forecasts.

In equities, London's blue chip FTSE 100 index finished almost unchanged on Thursday after a late U.S-inspired rally bucked up prices depressed earlier by fears over interest rate rises after the latest British inflation figures.
The FTSE 100 finished off just 0.8 points at 3,926.1 after an erratic session which saw shares hit lows of 3,904.

London had got off to a promising start bolstered by Wall Street's record-breaking overnight performance but stronger- than-expected British retail price data took the steam out of the rally and dragged shares down.
The data were described by one economist as "truly awful".

Frankfurt stocks ended late electronic dealings at a record high after Wall Street firmed. German government bond futures also hit new contract high after dollar strengthened against the mark, which is good for German exports.

A main feature of the German market was Commerzbank, which rose four percent as merger talk lifted the bank sector. The bank cooled speculation saying there was no one large buyer of shares. It said the boost came after an analyst presentation.
Frankfurt's 30-share IBIS DAX ended up 13.78 points at 2,784.39, just off intraday all-time high of 2,789.94 points.

On the Paris bourse French stocks closed virtually flat after briefly touching a new peak for the year in a day of very heavy trading which saw frenetic action in shares of insurers UAP and Axa as they requoted for the first time since announcing on Tuesday they planned to merge, creating the world's second largest insurance company.

UAP closed 16.34 percent higher at 136 francs, while Axa closed down 3.77 percent at 306.5 francs. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 0.99 points percent at 2218.18. Volume was an extremely heavy 9.9 billion francs ($1.95 billion).
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5095 marks and 111.20 yen compared with 1.5041 marks and 111.38 yen late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 0.8 points lower at 3,926.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 0.99 at 2,218.18.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 3.58 at 2,777.01.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed easier at $382.50 compared with $384.05 an ounce at the London close on Wednesday.
